# Results — Study 296 (Oscars-Effect) on the ^GSPC daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Oscar-ceremony dates and
Best Picture winners are hardcoded in [`data.py`](../oscars_effect/data.py) (67th–97th
ceremonies, 1995–2025, 31 events). S&P 500 daily price returns are ^GSPC via Yahoo
Finance, staged to `_cache/oscars_gspc_daily.parquet` (cache-first; the loader also
falls back to the repo-level `_cache/chinese_zodiac_GSPC_daily.parquet`). Match the
fingerprint below to confirm you hold the same data. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC daily (price-only, auto-adjusted close-to-close) | 1994-01-04 → 2026-06-12 | 8,165 sessions | `346fa83866ef` |
| Oscar-ceremony table | 67th–97th (1995–2025) | 31 ceremonies | hardcoded constant |

The event is the first **full trading session after** the broadcast (event day 0).
The ceremony airs Sunday/Monday evening US time, so day 0 is the earliest tradeable
reaction — one execution lag is baked in. The window runs relative days **-1 .. +3**.

## Primary spec — abnormal return on event day 0

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| n events | 31 |
| Event-day-0 mean return | **-23.8 bps** |
| Full-tape baseline daily mean | +4.1 bps |
| **Abnormal return** (event - baseline) | **-27.9 bps** |
| HAC (Newey-West) t-stat | **-1.35** |
| Plain t-stat | -1.13 |
| Event-day up-rate | 45.2% |
| Baseline up-rate | 54.0% |

The morning after the Oscars, the S&P 500 is, if anything, *slightly down* (-23.8 bps
mean, up only 45.2% of the time vs the 54.0% baseline) — but the HAC t-stat is **-1.35**,
comfortably inside the noise band. There is no statistically real reaction. The sign is
the opposite of the breathless "the market loves a winner" story, and it is not
significant in either direction.

## Cumulative abnormal return (CAR) profile

| rel_day | AAR (bps) | CAR (bps) | t |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| -1 | +26.8 | +26.8 | +1.67 |
| 0 | -27.9 | -1.1 | -1.32 |
| +1 | +19.4 | +18.3 | +0.74 |
| +2 | -8.5 | +9.8 | -0.59 |
| +3 | -20.7 | -10.9 | -1.22 |

The CAR wanders around zero across the whole window (final CAR = **-10.9 bps**); no
day clears |t| = 2. The largest single day is the run-up *before* the ceremony
(+26.8 bps, t = 1.67) — which, even if real, is unactionable since you cannot trade
on a result that has not been announced yet.

## Tradable rule — buy day-0, hold 1 session, net of costs

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| n trades | 31 |
| Gross mean per trade | -23.8 bps |
| One-way cost | 1.0 bps (entry + exit = 2.0 bps/trade) |
| **Net mean per trade** | **-25.8 bps** |
| HAC t on net per-trade return | **-1.46** |
| Buy-and-hold over the same exposed days | -23.8 bps |
| Cumulative net (31 trades) | -7.9% |
| Cumulative buy-and-hold (same days) | -7.3% |

The rule loses money *gross* before a cent of cost — there is no edge to harvest,
so costs only deepen the hole. Even buy-and-hold over exactly the same exposed days
is negative: the day-after-Oscars happens to be a mildly bad day historically, but
not reliably so.

## Permutation / placebo control

Drawing 5,000 random sets of 31 trading days and comparing their |mean abnormal
return| to the observed one:

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| Observed abnormal | -27.9 bps |
| Two-sided placebo p | **0.183** |
| Fraction of placebos below the observed mean | 9.3% |

A random set of 31 days produces a swing this large or larger **18.3%** of the time —
the real event-day mean is an ordinary draw, not a tail event.

## Positive control (synthetic tape)

Planting a one-day post-ceremony bump in a synthetic random walk and re-running the
event-day test confirms the machinery detects a real effect when one exists:

| planted bump (bps) | abnormal (bps) | event HAC t |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 | +5.1 | +0.40 |
| 50 | +54.9 | +3.16 |
| 150 | +154.5 | +8.69 |
| 300 | +304.0 | +16.98 |

The engine is sensitive to a ~50 bps planted effect at n = 29–31. The real tape shows
**nothing** of that magnitude — the null is not a power failure, it is a true absence.

## The n = 31 problem

There have been only 31 ceremonies inside the clean ^GSPC window. With ~110 bps daily
S&P vol, the minimum detectable one-day mean at |t| = 2 with n = 31 is roughly
`2 × 110 / sqrt(31) ≈ 40 bps`. The observed abnormal return (-27.9 bps) is well inside
that band, and in the *wrong* direction for the folklore. Even if a true ±20 bps Oscar
effect existed, n = 31 could never resolve it.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Event-day-0 abnormal return -27.9 bps, HAC t = -1.35, placebo
  p = 0.18; no day in the -1..+3 window clears |t| = 2; the CAR wanders around zero.
  The reaction is statistically indistinguishable from noise, and what little sign
  there is runs *opposite* to the "market cheers the winner" story. n = 31 is too
  small to detect anything below ~40 bps.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The day-after rule loses money gross (-23.8 bps/trade)
  before costs, and costs only make it worse (-25.8 bps net). There is no vehicle and
  no edge — buy-and-hold over the same days is also negative.
- **The market does not care who wins Best Picture.** The Oscars move red carpets and
  studio share prices at the margins, but the broad index registers nothing the next
  morning beyond ordinary daily noise.
